title: BlueStone Stock Surges 20% After Third Straight Profitable Quarter
excerpt: The omnichannel jewellery retailer posted ₹6 crore net profit in Q1 FY27 on 49% revenue growth, hitting the upper circuit as investor confidence strengthens.
body:
Shares of BlueStone Jewellery and Lifestyle locked in the 20% upper circuit at ₹732.45 on the NSE on Tuesday after the Bengaluru-based omnichannel jewellery retailer posted its third consecutive quarterly profit, reinforcing a turnaround narrative that has drawn sustained investor interest since its stock exchange debut last year.

The Accel-backed company reported a net profit of ₹6 crore in Q1 FY27, swinging from a net loss of ₹34.8 crore in the same quarter a year ago. On a sequential basis, however, profit after tax declined 80% from the ₹31 crore recorded in Q4 FY26, reflecting seasonal patterns in jewellery demand.

"Customers are price-point driven, not investment-driven; stable gold prices are the most conducive environment for us to achieve our growth targets."

— BlueStone management, post-earnings call

Revenue and Margins Accelerate

Operating revenue grew 49% year-on-year to ₹737 crore, up from ₹493 crore in Q1 FY26. The growth came despite customs duty on gold rising from 6% to 15%, according to CEO Gaurav Singh Kushwaha, who credited product design and pricing flexibility for maintaining demand.

Same-store sales growth came in at 39%, with older store cohorts performing at similar or better levels. Reported EBITDA nearly doubled to ₹110 crore from ₹57 crore a year ago, while pre-Ind AS EBITDA more than doubled to ₹55 crore, pushing the margin to 7.5% — an expansion of 273 basis points. Standalone cash profit stood at ₹57 crore, underscoring what the company described as a self-funded growth model.

Expansion Into Smaller Cities

BlueStone added 12 new stores during the quarter, taking its total count to 352 across 139 cities. The company entered five new markets, all in Tier II and Tier III cities, where nearly half its stores now operate. Kushwaha told The Economic Times that stores generally turn profitable within two to three months of opening.

"We were online-only for the first six or seven years. Then we realised that while online lets customers explore designs, for conversions, stores still work very well."

— Gaurav Singh Kushwaha, CEO, BlueStone

Almost 95% of BlueStone's products are manufactured in-house, which the company says gives it a 300–400 basis point cost advantage over competitors that outsource production while also protecting design intellectual property.

Repeat customers now account for roughly 60% of revenue, with average order values from returning buyers running 20–30% higher than from new customers. New customer acquisition dipped to 40,000 from 50,000 on a quarter-on-quarter basis, attributed to merchandising disruptions from gold price swings.

What Lies Ahead

BlueStone has set aggressive medium-term targets: 706 stores and ₹12,000 crore in annual revenue by FY30, roughly five times its FY26 revenue of ₹2,486 crore. The company expects EBITDA margins to expand from the current 7.5% to about 15% over the next four years as revenue scales.

The stock, which listed in August 2025 at ₹510 — a 1.3% discount to its issue price of ₹517 — has now gained over 40% from its debut. Market capitalisation stood at ₹11,082 crore, or approximately $1.15 billion, at Tuesday's close of ₹727.20 on the BSE.

JM Financial maintains a 'Buy' rating with a target price of ₹650, citing a consumer shift from wedding jewellery to lifestyle pieces as a structural tailwind for organised players. Nuvama has also flagged improving unit economics and the expanding store network as key drivers. Kushwaha said the $80–90 billion jewellery market could grow to $120–140 billion in four to five years, offering ample room for multiple organised players to scale.
